title: Model Version Sunset & Migration Playbook (customer notices, migration docs, automation)
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create an operational playbook and collateral for sunsetting older model versions in the Redwood catalog. This ticket covers the end-to-end flow: automated notices to customers, migration guidance and sample prompts, API deprecation headers, UI warnings in Console, and monitoring/rollback criteria. The goal is to reduce customer surprise, minimize regressions, and provide clear opt-in migration paths for users who need to pin legacy behavior.
background: We maintain multiple model variants and occasionally need to remove older weights or quantized builds due to performance regressions, licensing changes, or maintenance cost. Historically these sunsets have caused confusion: customers who pinned implicitly (no explicit pinning field) suddenly saw behavior changes or outages. We now have version pinning semantics across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. This project standardizes notice cadence, migration artifacts, and automation for safe sunsets.
goals: Standardize a 3-phase notice cadence: Early Notice (60 days), Final Notice (14 days), and Sunset Day (0 days)
Publish migration guides with sample prompts, token-comparison checklist, and recommended replacement model variants
Automate generation of deprecation headers and Console banners tied to model version metadata
Create monitoring dashboards to detect customer usage pinned to a retiring version and track migration progress
Provide rollback/fallback rules and SLO adjustments for affected customers
acceptance_criteria: A single Playbook doc exists in Confluence with step-by-step deprecation workflow
Notice templates (email, banner, API header) are available in the repo and can be parameterized
Console displays a prominent banner when a pinned model version is scheduled for sunset
Automation task that compiles a list of customers using the version (Hosted + Dedicated) runs and outputs CSV
Monitoring dashboard shows pinned-version user counts and migration rates over time
All stakeholder sign-offs obtained: PM, Eng runtime, Design, Reliability, Legal for licensing-sensitive models
rollout_steps: 1) Finalize Playbook doc and templates; link to Confluence page: https://confluence.redwood.ai/model-sunset-playbook
2) ENG: Add deprecation metadata fields to model catalog (deprecation_date, notice_start_date, replacement_model) - ENG-2198
3) ENG: API returns Deprecation headers (X-Model-Deprecation, X-Model-Replacement) for requests against deprecated versions - ENG-2104
4) Design: Create Console banner patterns and banner approval flow - DES-457
5) PM: Run outreach plan for top 50 customers (account teams + customer success)
6) Automation: weekly job to export pinned-version usage and email stakeholders
7) Publish migration guide + example prompts and a token-cost comparison matrix in Drive
8) 60-day Early Notice: send soft notice + add Console info panel
9) 14-day Final Notice: email + in-console banner + API Deprecation header enforcement
10) Sunset Day: disable model in Hosted catalog (with clear 0-day fallback rules for Dedicated/Private) and publish post-mortem checklist
notice_templates:
Early Notice (60 days):
Subject: Planned Sunset of model-version vX.Y — Action recommended
Body: We are planning to retire model 'redwood/xyz-vX.Y' on DATE (60 days). Recommended replacement: redwood/xyz-vX.Z. See migration guide: <link>. If you have pinned this exact version, please test the replacement. Reach out to your CSM or support@redwood.ai for exemptions.

Final Notice (14 days):
Subject: Final Notice — model-version vX.Y will be retired in 14 days
Body: This is a final reminder that 'redwood/xyz-vX.Y' will be removed on DATE. After that date requests that specify this exact version will receive 410 + migration instructions. To avoid disruption, update your pin to 'redwood/xyz-vX.Z' or remove version pinning to use the catalog default. If you require extended access, contact support.

Sunset Day Notice (0 days):
Subject: Model-version vX.Y retired today
Body: 'redwood/xyz-vX.Y' has been removed from our hosted catalog. Calls that referenced this version may fail; compatible fallback rules will attempt replacement if configured. See migration log and rollback options: <link>
monitoring: Dashboard: 'Pinned Version Usage' showing daily active keys by pinned version
Metric: pinned_user_count{version} exported to Observability with alert if >50 active keys 7 days before sunset
Metric: migration_rate (percent of pinned customers migrated to replacement)
SLO impact sheet to be generated for top-10 affected customers
communication_channels: Status page announcement for large or breaking sunsets
open_questions: What is the minimum notice period for models with third-party license constraints? (Legal to confirm)
Do Dedicated customers expect the same automation or must account teams coordinate extended windows?
Should we automatically map pinned legacy quantized builds to quantized replacements or require manual opt-in?
What is the default fallback behavior in Private deployments where Redwood cannot disable a model?
